title: Canadian economy lost 68,000 jobs in September
summary: The decline marks a second straight month of job losses. Economists polled ahead of the release predicted employers added 9,200 positions in September.

image.caption: Employment-seekers line up for a chance to interview at the CNE job fair, held at the Enercare Centre, in Toronto, on July 29, 2026. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: The decline marks a second straight month of job losses. Economists polled ahead of the release predicted employers added 9,200 positions in September.
Decline comes after economy shed 42,000 jobs the month before
Canada lost 68,000 jobs in September, according to Statistics Canada, marking a second month of losses in a row, while the unemployment rate rose to 6.5 per cent.
The decline was concentrated in youth aged 15 to 24, who accounted for 48,000 job losses, according to the data agency.
Statistics Canada says job losses were split between full- and part-time work and were concentrated in the public sector.

By sector, educational services, health care and social assistance, and manufacturing led the declines. More workers in "other services," which includes things like repair and maintenance, offset the losses.
A Reuters poll of economists ahead of the release predicted employers added 9,200 positions in September.
The decline follows 42,000 job losses in August, which came as a surprise to economists and snapped a hot streak for the labour market.

Before the two monthly declines, Statistics Canada data showed employment trending upward, with 181,000 jobs added between April and July. Employment is still up compared to a year ago by 95,000 positions.
The jobs data will be the Bank of Canada's last look at the labour market before its next interest rate decision on Oct. 28.
With files from the Canadian Press
